content.thinking:
I need to correct myself: the error rate actually dropped slightly, so the real impact was latency, not errors. The root cause traces to the 22:13 deploy that changed the cache port in the production values file, making the cache unreachable so every account-page request stalled on a failed connection before falling back to origin.

For the summary, I want to keep it accessible — avoiding internal component names, referring generically to "account pages" and "an internal data store" — and note that the automated rollback restored baseline within minutes, with a draft PR already filed.

On assumptions, I should flag that the latency attribution rests on correlating deploy timing, that the second candidate cause was never actually tested, and that I'm treating the rollback as causal because metrics recovered afterward rather than confirming it directly. I'll also note I haven't independently verified the cache was healthy on its original port, and that the disconnect errors are likely unrelated noise. I can still reference the 22:13–22:19 window since that's given data, just without implying I computed it myself.

assumptions: The rollback is assumed to be what restored service: metrics returned to baseline shortly after it was applied, but no separate control was run to confirm the recovery was not coincidental.

The cache service itself was assumed healthy and listening on its original port; this was inferred from the config diff and the 'connection refused' errors rather than verified directly against the cache.
The alternative hypothesis — that the cache dependency itself failed — was never tested, only judged less likely than the config diff.
The steady stream of ClientDisconnected errors on account pages runs from well before the onset through the whole window and is treated as pre-existing background noise, not part of this incident.
Customer impact is inferred from latency and cache-hit metrics; no user reports, session data, or downstream business signals were consulted.
The change-event history was read for the 24 hours before onset only, so any earlier contributing change would not have been seen.
input.executive_summary: Between 22:13 and 22:19 UTC on 28 September 2026, the account pages of the online shop became noticeably slow to load — typical page responses went from near-instant to several times slower. Requests still completed: the share of failing requests did not rise above its normal level during the window, so the customer-visible effect was delay rather than errors, limited to shoppers loading account pages in that roughly six-minute stretch. The cause was a settings change that went out with a routine software update and pointed the service at the wrong address for the short-term data store it normally reads from. Because that store could not be reached, every page request first waited on a failed connection attempt and then rebuilt the data the slow way. The automated on-call system detected the slowdown, traced it to the update, reversed the update, and confirmed performance had returned to normal. A draft code change to prevent a recurrence has been opened for review.
input.root_cause: A deploy of io-shop at 22:13Z shipped a bad config value in deploy/values-production.yaml, changing the io-summary-cache endpoint port from 6379 to 6380; with nothing listening on 6380, every account-page request burned time on a refused connection to redis://cache.io-shop.svc.cluster.local:6380 before falling back to the uncached path, collapsing cache_hit_ratio to zero and pushing p50/p95 latency from roughly 26ms to roughly 190ms. Request volume and CPU limits were flat across the window and the rollout had fully converged, ruling out saturation, autoscaling, and split-version effects.
